--- title: "Number morphology (pseudowords)" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · L_ORAL_MF_STX_MORFOLOGIA_NUMERO_PSEUDOPAL" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea L_ORAL_MF_STX_MORFOLOGIA_NUMERO_PSEUDOPAL`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Morfología de número (pseudopalabras)*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/L_ORAL_MF_STX_MORFOLOGIA_NUMERO_PSEUDOPAL.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Number morphology (pseudowords), at age 6 (2,288 administrations in 3 cohorts). AUC .62–.62 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 196 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | forced choice | | Items | 5 | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The experimenter says a verb name, then child makes the verb agree in number with the person(s) performing an action in the picture presented on the screen. | ![Example of the screen format (2018 screenshot; not necessarily an item from this task).](../../figuras/pantallas/formato_decision.png){width=45%} ## Theoretical framework These tasks measure **morphological and syntactic knowledge of oral language**: inflecting words and pseudowords for gender, number and tense, ordering words to form a sentence, and choosing the picture that matches a sentence. With pseudowords, the child has to apply the rule because they cannot rely on a known word. In the simple view of reading they are part of language comprehension [@hoover1990simple]. **What the evidence says:** - **Morphology is related to reading, also in the long term.** A meta-analysis of 44 studies finds a correlation of .57 between morphological awareness and reading comprehension [@liu2023morphological]. Another, with 35 longitudinal studies, estimates .48 with later word reading and .55 with comprehension, more with accuracy than with fluency [@bodynek2026longitudinal]. - **In Spanish, morphology helps comprehension, not decoding.** In Grade 4 its effect on comprehension is only direct and does not go through word reading, because grapheme–phoneme rules are enough for pronunciation [@dalessio2019morphological]. In 234 Grade 4 children from Seville, syntax predicted comprehension after controlling for decoding and vocabulary; morphology added nothing [@simpson2020morphological]. - **Syntax has a role of its own.** Syntactic awareness in Grade 3 predicts progress in reading comprehension up to Grade 4, but not word reading [@deacon2018syntactic]. Language at age 3½, grammar included, predicts comprehension at age 8½ [@hulme2015foundations]. Almost all the evidence comes from children aged 8 to 10. There is little in Spanish with oral tasks at ages 4–6, the ages of our tasks. **What our data show.** These are class B and C tasks, with few items. - **Low consistency and stability.** α = .57–.71. Stability across terms is very low: ρ = .22 for gender and .05 for number with words. - **Ceiling and floor.** 48% of 6-year-olds get everything right in gender with pseudowords; 25% get nothing right in number with pseudowords. - **What predicts best.** Grammatical reception and sentence ordering: AUC .63–.69 against the reading difficulty label and .57–.66 against later low comprehension. Morphology with words stays close to chance (AUC .45–.62). They are best used as complementary information on oral language, not for individual screening. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 6.1| 2010| 152|2016/17 | 916| 263| 652| 34| | 6.1| 2011| 183|2017/18 | 775| 0| 775| 31| | 6.2| 2013| 903|2019/20 | 597| 380| 217| 31| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 6.1| 263| 2010| 1.79| 1.50| 2| 0.42| 26.24| 4.94| | 6.2| 380| 2013| 1.78| 1.48| 2| 0.49| 24.74| 4.74| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–5 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 6.1| 263|0–5 |0–5 |0–5 | | | 6.2| 380|0–5 |0–5 |0–5 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). α (2021) = .60. ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Oral morphosyntax (6.1, r = .39); Verbal memory (6.2, r = .34). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .62–.62. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .57–.63. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_MF_STX_MORFOLOGIA_NUMERO_PSEUDOPAL_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .59–.65 (2 time points; 198–507 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 6.1| 263| 2010| 0| 0| 0| 0| 2| 3| 4| | 6.2| 380| 2013| 0| 0| 0| 1| 2| 3| 4| **Floor effect.** At 6.1 and 6.2 P10 coincides with the worst possible score (at 6.1, P25 too): many children are tied at the minimum and the norms do not distinguish between them. At those time points this task cannot be used to grade difficulty. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_MF_STX_MORFOLOGIA_NUMERO_PSEUDOPAL_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 6.1| 1,678| 0.088| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.1| 1,686| 0.132| 0.007| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.1| 1,681| 0.020| 0.421| |School (ICC) | 6.1| 1,691| 0.103| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.2| 597| 0.154| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.2| 595| 0.116| 0.156| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 597| 0.014| 0.735| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 597| 0.273| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Number morphology (pseudowords)” (code 196; LEEDUCA battery) assesses inflectional morphology. The child selects a response among the options presented on the screen. It comprises 5 items. The time limit is 90 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011 and 2013 cohorts it was administered in 3 sessions, from 6 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .60 (N = 2,293, 5 items). Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .57–.63. ## Pending issues - Floor effect at 6.1, 6.2 (more than 15% with zero correct). - Floor effect in the norms at 6.1 and 6.2: at least 10% of children have the worst possible score, so P10 does not exist. At those time points the "severe" and "very severe" levels must not be assigned with this task (study M3). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
